==English==

===Etymology===
{{bor+|en|gmw-msc|wraith}}, first attested in 1513 in a translation of the ''[[Aeneid]]''.<ref>{{cite-book|title={{w|Eneados}}|year=1513|volume=10|translator={{w|Gavin Douglas|Gawin Douglas}}|chapter=X|section=lines 81–82|passage=Nor ȝit na vayn wrathys nor gaiſtis quent / Thi char conſtrenyt bakwart forto went|translation=Nor yet no vain wraiths nor quaint ghosts / constrained Thy chariot to go backward}}
</ref><ref>{{cite-book|title={{w|Eneados}}|year=1513|volume=10|translator={{w|Gavin Douglas|Gawin Douglas}}|chapter=XI|section=lines 95–96|passage=Syklyke as that, thai ſay, in diuers placis / The wraithis walkis of goiſtis that ar ded|translation=Such as that, they say, in diverse places / The wraiths walk of ghosts that are dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite-book|title={{w|Eneados}}|year=1513|volume=10|translator={{w|Gavin Douglas|Gawin Douglas}}|chapter=XI|section=lines 129–130|passage=Thydder went this wrath or ſchaddo of Ene, / That ſemyt, all abaſyt, faſt to fle|translation=Thither went this wraith or shade of Ene, / That seemed, all abased, fast to flee}}</ref>

The word has {{unk|en|no certain etymology}}; it may be a transferred use of {{cog|gmw-msc|wraith}}, {{m|gmw-msc|wrath|pos=nominally "anger, rage", adjectivally "angry, wrathful"}}, thus connecting it to {{m|en|writhe}} and making it a {{doublet|en|wrath|wroth|nocap=1}}. 

The old ''Century Dictionary'' compares {{cog|non|vǫrðr|t=guardian}}. <!-- source? cite the work, not just a bare surname. // Klein compares {{cog|ga|arracht|t=apparition}}, which is related to {{m|ga|riocht|t=shape, likeness}}. -->

===Pronunciation===
* {{enPR|rāth}}, {{IPA|en|/ɹeɪθ/}}
* {{rhymes|en|eɪθ|s=1}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-wraith.ogg|a=US}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}

# A [[ghost#Noun|ghost]] or [[specter]], especially a person's [[likeness]] seen just after their [[death]].
#: {{synonyms|en|Thesaurus:ghost}}
#* {{RQ:Burroughs Princess of Mars|chapter=Sola Tells Me Her Story|pages=159–160|pageref=159|passage=We might indeed have been the '''wraiths''' of the departed dead upon the dead sea of that dying planet for all the sound or sign we made in passing.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|passage=Like '''wraiths''' with the impediments of bodies they stumbled in the direction of Salthill faces.
|title=Middle Age: A Romance
|year=2001
|author=w:Joyce Carol Oates
|publisher=Fourth Estate
|edition=paperback
|page=80}}
